F1.quote: The IISH manages a rich collection in the field of socio-economic history that is made available online and in the reading room as much as possible.
F1.claim: the institute manages a collection in socio-economic history, made available online and in the reading room 'as much as possible'
F1.lineage: the collections: their measure and their kinds

F2.quote: The archives, publications and audiovisual collections cover more than 50 kilometres and offer (historical) information on organisations and persons in the field of labour and social and emancipatory movements.
F2.claim: its archives, publications and audiovisual collections cover more than 50 kilometres and inform on organisations and persons of labour and social and emancipatory movements
F2.lineage: the collections: their measure and their kinds

F3.quote: Read about our research programme here; our four research clusters Global Labour Relations, Commodities, Environment and Labour, Social and Economic Inequality and Individual and Collective Action.
F3.claim: a research programme in four clusters (the page's names)

F4.quote: View our thousands of datasets on demography, wages, life courses, inequality, prices, and labour relations here. The IISH is one of the world's leading data centres on socio-economic history.
F4.claim: thousands of datasets on demography, wages, life courses, inequality, prices and labour relations; one of the world's leading data centres on socio-economic history

F5.quote: View the latest IISH news items and events here, as well as information about our workshops, the European Social Science History Conference (ESSHC) and the Thesis Prize.
F5.claim: it organizes workshops, the European Social Science History Conference (ESSHC) and a Thesis Prize

F6.quote: An Institute of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences
F6.claim: an institute of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences
F6.lineage: who holds it: the academy, its cluster and the foundation

F7.quote: The Reading Room is open Monday - Thursday: 09:00 to 17:00
F7.claim: the reading room is open Monday to Thursday, 09:00 to 17:00

F9.quote: The International Institute of Social History ( IISH ; Dutch : Internationaal Instituut voor Sociale Geschiedenis , IISG ) is one of the largest archives of labor and social history in the world.
F9.claim: one of the largest archives of labor and social history in the world
F9.lineage: what it is: an archive and research institute of labour and social history
F9.date: undated revision (the article as fetched 2026-10-31; its counts 'As of 2000')

F10.quote: Located in Amsterdam , its one million volumes and 5,445 archival collections include the papers of major figures and institutions in radical leftist thought.
F10.claim: in Amsterdam; one million volumes and 5,445 archival collections, including papers of major figures and institutions of radical leftist thought
F10.lineage: the papers it holds: organizations and persons of the movements
F10.date: undated revision (the article as fetched 2026-10-31; its counts 'As of 2000')

F11.quote: The IISH was founded in 1935 by Nicolaas Posthumus as an independent scientific institute. It is part of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences .
F11.claim: founded in 1935 by Nicolaas Posthumus as an independent scientific institute; part of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences
F11.lineage: founding: 1935, Posthumus, a history from the 1920s
F11.date: undated revision (the article as fetched 2026-10-31; its counts 'As of 2000')

F12.quote: The International Institute of Social History specializes in international labor and social history, including that of the Netherlands. As of 2000, it holds one million volumes, 80,000 audiovisual items, 2,400 serials, three million digital files, and 30,000 linear feet of manuscripts across 5,445 collections.
F12.claim: it specializes in international labor and social history; as of 2000, one million volumes, 80,000 audiovisual items, 2,400 serials, three million digital files and 30,000 linear feet of manuscripts in 5,445 collections
F12.lineage: the collections: their measure and their kinds
F12.date: undated revision (the article as fetched 2026-10-31; its counts 'As of 2000')

F13.quote: Among the latter are institutional collections from Amnesty International , Confederación Nacional del Trabajo and Federación Anarquista Ibérica , the European Trade Union Confederation , Freedom Press , Greenpeace International , the International Confederation of Free Trade Unions , Russian Socialist Revolutionary Party , Socialist International , and the personal papers of Emma Goldman , Karl Marx , Max Nettlau , Lev Trotsky , Karl Kautsky , Ernest Mandel , and Sylvia Pankhurst .
F13.claim: institutional collections (Amnesty International, the CNT and FAI, the ETUC, Freedom Press, Greenpeace International, the ICFTU, the Russian Socialist Revolutionary Party, the Socialist International) and the personal papers of Goldman, Marx, Nettlau, Trotsky, Kautsky, Mandel and Pankhurst
F13.lineage: the papers it holds: organizations and persons of the movements
F13.date: undated revision (the article as fetched 2026-10-31; its counts 'As of 2000')

F14.quote: The institute is the foremost repository of anarchist documents in the world.
F14.claim: the foremost repository of anarchist documents in the world (two references)
F14.lineage: the papers it holds: organizations and persons of the movements
F14.date: undated revision (the article as fetched 2026-10-31; its counts 'As of 2000')

F15.quote: Nicolaas Posthumus , a socialist and first chair appointment in economic history in the Netherlands, … founded the International Institute of Social History in 1935. … To examine how labour relations develop over time, IISG collected archives from all over the world. During the first years Posthumus succeeded in obtaining many papers from anarchists ( Bakunin manuscripts), other socialist and social democratic and Marxist movements from Germany and Russia.
F15.claim: Posthumus, a socialist and the Netherlands' first chair in economic history, founded it; to examine how labour relations develop it collected archives worldwide, in its first years papers of anarchists (the Bakunin manuscripts) and of socialist, social democratic and Marxist movements of Germany and Russia
F15.lineage: founding: 1935, Posthumus, a history from the 1920s
F15.date: undated revision (the article as fetched 2026-10-31; its counts 'As of 2000')

F16.quote: Before the Germans invaded the Netherlands in May 1940, Posthumus was able to move the most valuable archives to London. During the war, most remaining IISG archives were transported to Nazi Germany between June 1942 and September 1944 by agents of the Reichsleiter Rosenberg Taskforce led by Eberhard Kautter .
F16.claim: before May 1940 the most valuable archives went to London; most of the rest were taken to Nazi Germany, 1942–1944, by the Reichsleiter Rosenberg Taskforce
F16.lineage: rescue: archives brought to safety, seized and returned
F16.date: undated revision (the article as fetched 2026-10-31; its counts 'As of 2000')

F17.quote: They were not destroyed, but stored for eventual inclusion in the Advanced School of the NSDAP . … Most of the papers were rediscovered in Hannover in 1946, and some other parts were later found in archives in Moscow in 1991, and returned to Amsterdam.
F17.claim: the seized archives were stored for the Advanced School of the NSDAP, mostly rediscovered in Hannover in 1946, other parts found in Moscow archives in 1991 and returned to Amsterdam
F17.lineage: rescue: archives brought to safety, seized and returned
F17.date: undated revision (the article as fetched 2026-10-31; its counts 'As of 2000')

F18.quote: In 1989 the International Institute of Social History moved to new premises: an old warehouse at the Cruquiusweg in the eastern part of Amsterdam.
F18.claim: since 1989 in an old warehouse on the Cruquiusweg, eastern Amsterdam
F18.date: undated revision (the article as fetched 2026-10-31; its counts 'As of 2000')

F19.quote: IISG hosts part of the IHLIA LGBT Heritage collection (LGBT Archives).
F19.claim: it hosts part of the IHLIA LGBT Heritage collection
F19.lineage: the papers it holds: organizations and persons of the movements
F19.date: undated revision (the article as fetched 2026-10-31; its counts 'As of 2000')

F21.quote: The IISG is a leading international archive and research institute in the field of social history, the history of labour and social movements.
F21.claim: the academy: a leading international archive and research institute of social history, the history of labour and social movements
F21.lineage: what it is: an archive and research institute of labour and social history

F22.quote: Since its foundation in 1935, the institute has built up one of the world's largest socio-economic history collections and conducted research on social inequality, globalisation, the environment and migration.
F22.claim: since 1935 one of the world's largest socio-economic history collections; research on social inequality, globalisation, the environment and migration

F23.quote: The IISG cooperates with the Huygens Institute and the Meertens Institute in the Academy's Humanities Cluster (HuC) .
F23.claim: it cooperates with the Huygens and Meertens Institutes in the Academy's Humanities Cluster
F23.lineage: who holds it: the academy, its cluster and the foundation

F24.quote: The International Institute of Social History was founded in the turbulent 1930s at a time when, following Hitler’s seizure of power, many documents and archives of opposition movements were threatened with becoming irredeemably lost.
F24.claim: founded in the 1930s, when after Hitler's seizure of power the archives of opposition movements were threatened with loss
F24.lineage: founding: 1935, Posthumus, a history from the 1920s
F24.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31; site copyright 2016-2026)

F25.quote: Vital archives that were brought to safety in Amsterdam in the early years include: the archive of the German socialist movement (including the manuscripts of Marx and Engels), the archives of revolutionaries at risk from Stalin, and the archives of the Spanish trade unions, threatened with falling into Franco’s hands.
F25.claim: archives brought to safety in Amsterdam: the German socialist movement's (with the manuscripts of Marx and Engels), those of revolutionaries at risk from Stalin, and the Spanish trade unions' threatened by Franco
F25.lineage: rescue: archives brought to safety, seized and returned
F25.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31; site copyright 2016-2026)

F26.quote: After the end of World War Two, the IISH successfully continued collecting documents. With the exception of Dutch emancipation movements such as Provo, and internationally active movements such as Greenpeace and Amnesty International, endangered archives of organizations and individuals from countries like Turkey, Iran, Burma and Indonesia were safely housed at the Institute.
F26.claim: after 1945 it kept collecting: Dutch emancipation movements such as Provo, Greenpeace and Amnesty International, and endangered archives from Turkey, Iran, Burma and Indonesia
F26.lineage: rescue: archives brought to safety, seized and returned
F26.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31; site copyright 2016-2026)

F27.quote: The total archival collection includes over 5,000 collections. Archives and archival finding aids can be searched on this website (or in the catalogue ). Descriptions of Dutch archives are in Dutch; others are in English.
F27.claim: over 5,000 archival collections, searchable with their finding aids; Dutch archives described in Dutch, others in English
F27.lineage: the collections: their measure and their kinds
F27.date: undated (the page as fetched 2026-10-31; site copyright 2016-2026)

F28.quote: The IISH is a unique institute, serving science and society on a global scale. At an international level, we generate and offer reliable information and insights about the (long-term) origins, effects and consequences of social inequality.
F28.claim: its mission: information and insight on the long-term origins, effects and consequences of social inequality
F28.lineage: mission: social inequality and the heritage of oppressed movements

F29.quote: To promote this, we form an international hub for social historians worldwide. We offer and produce historical sources and data, facilitate social-history research and collaborate internationally in ground breaking research projects.
F29.claim: an international hub for social historians; sources and data; collaboration in research
F29.lineage: mission: social inequality and the heritage of oppressed movements

F30.quote: Moreover, by preserving the heritage of often oppressed social movements, the Institute serves the quality of the world's memory. With our work we hope to contribute to a vibrant civil society.
F30.claim: by preserving the heritage of often oppressed social movements it serves the quality of the world's memory
F30.lineage: mission: social inequality and the heritage of oppressed movements

F31.quote: Established in 1935, the IISH is one of the world's leading research institutes on social history. Since 1979 the IISH has been an institute of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW).
F31.claim: established 1935; an institute of the KNAW since 1979
F31.lineage: who holds it: the academy, its cluster and the foundation

F32.quote: The collections, some of which concern politically sensitive materials, are the property of or have been issued on standing loan to the independent IISH Foundation.
F32.claim: the collections, some politically sensitive, are owned by, or on standing loan to, the independent IISH Foundation
F32.lineage: who holds it: the academy, its cluster and the foundation

F33.locus: General: Can I conduct research at the IISH / NEHA?
F33.quote: The International Institute of Social History (including the Press Collection of The Netherlands Institute for Sound & Vision) and the Netherlands Economic History Archive welcome everyone to the reading room to do their own research. In addition, we provide online access to large parts of the collection via our online catalogue. We want to create as few barriers as possible for people to use our collections.
F33.claim: the IISH (with the Press Collection of the Netherlands Institute for Sound & Vision) and the Netherlands Economic History Archive welcome everyone to the reading room; online access to large parts; 'as few barriers as possible'

F34.quote: Access to the reading room and consulting the collections are free of charge.

F35.locus: Consulting: Can archival documents be viewed online?
F35.quote: The IISH manages more than 5,000 different archival collections. Of these, about ten percent (nearly 500 archives) can be consulted online.
F35.claim: more than 5,000 archival collections, about ten percent (nearly 500) online
F35.lineage: the collections: their measure and their kinds

F36.locus: Consulting: Are all archival documents accessible without restrictions?
F36.quote: In principle, most archives are available for research without restrictions. Some archives are not freely available for consultation. These are usually archives where there is a contractual stipulation that the donor or lender of the archive must give permission for consultation, scans and/or publication.
F36.claim: most archives are open; some are restricted by a contractual stipulation that the donor or lender must permit consultation, scans or publication

F37.quote: The IISG mediates in obtaining permission to view archives that are restricted.
F37.claim: the institute mediates permission to view restricted archives

F38.quote: The material at the IISH must be available to everyone. For this reason, we do not lend our items.
F38.claim: nothing is lent, so that the material stays available to everyone

F39.locus: Other: Karl Marx's original Communist Manifesto
F39.quote: No, unfortunately we do not have the opportunity to show visitors Marx's original writings. We do offer his archive, designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site, fully digitized in our catalogue.
F39.claim: Marx's original writings are not shown to visitors; his archive, a UNESCO World Heritage designation, is fully digitized in the catalogue
F39.lineage: the papers it holds: organizations and persons of the movements

F40.quote: All material is stored in stacks that are closed to the public at our Cruquiusweg location in Amsterdam.
F40.claim: all material is kept in closed stacks at Cruquiusweg, Amsterdam
